correctness.rationale: The cyclic subgroup generated by an element of H_i is exactly L_i×C_q; subgroup containment yields precisely the stated twin cliques and A_i−H_i and H_i−C cross edges. Two initially white members of any twin class cannot receive a first force separating them. For profiles with at most one white per class, each single-white branch clears from a blue A_i, which exists since p is odd. If there is no double branch, any residual singleton white in C clears from a blue H_i. If exactly one branch is double-white, an all-blue different branch can first force a white C (there are t≥2 branches); C then forces the remaining white H_i and the final A_i follows. If at least two branches are double-white, the white A_i/H_i pairs in those branches form a fort: every vertex outside it sees zero or at least two of its vertices, so no earlier move can circumvent the obstruction. Writing N=p^d q−1, c=q−1, s=q(p−1) and h=(p−1)(q−1), the weighted white enumerator is (1+cz)[(1+sz)^t+t(p−1)h z²(1+sz)^{t−1}]; u^N times this at z=1/u gives the exact polynomial, and its largest white size t+2 gives the asserted minimum profiles and multiplicity. In the indefinite Gram representation, the assigned vectors span the stated t+2 dimensions (recover g=(e_i+w)−e_i−f), the form is nondegenerate, and the pairings match exactly the edges; hence the witness really has rank t+2. The standard M≤Z bound completes both rank and nullity claims. Independently rebuilt the two d=2 graphs by cyclic-subgroup containment and tested all 512 and 8192 representative profiles, obtaining Z=38,66 and weighted minimum counts 256000,95551488. The uploaded verify.py was inspected, not executed; those bounded independent checks do not prove the general identity.
residual_risks: The proof uses odd p and q to ensure usable blue representatives in each one-white class. No extension to singleton blow-up classes or higher group exponents is assumed.

Standard lexicographic/corona product comparisons inspect scalar forcing or maximal failed sets, not the explicit quotient enumerator.

evidence: If the quotient has t−1 initially blue vertices at optimum, the earlier transfer gives Z=N−(2t+1)+(t−1)=N−t−2, and mr=t+2. The loop quotient indeed has largest successful white set t+2: one per arm, an extra white in one arm, plus the center. The same-size set count requires the choices distinguishing single from double arms and multiplication by the actual class sizes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This proves mechanical coverage for the scalar transfer from the quotient; it does not produce the entire weighted enumerator without the exact graph-specific successful-set classification. Boyer defines the target polynomial, and Tóth supplies the line count, but neither inspected passage supplies that classification.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The twin reduction is prior, including its equivalence at the profile level. The general equivalence is not the explicit successful-subset enumeration of this subdivided star: the forbidden coexistence of two double-white arms and its factored count must still be determined in that quotient. Resultary 05266193a935's private clique decoration is not the shared-center nonuniform blow-up.

value.rationale: The shared q-core couples projectively many arms, and the exact one-double-arm limit explains which white configurations survive globally. The factored enumerator and minimum-set count specify information not given by a scalar rank or by previously studied domination. They avoid subset enumeration in a natural infinite proper-power family; the scalar equality alone would not justify the contribution given the earlier blow-up theorem.
residual_risks: No claim is made that the enumerator extends directly to singleton classes or more general p-primary group structure.
